what_its_for: Sulconazole nitrate is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal skin infections. It works against conditions like ringworm (tinea corporis), jock itch (tinea cruris), athlete's foot (tinea pedis), and a skin condition called tinea versicolor, which causes patchy skin color changes. It kills the fungus causing your infection by destroying the fungal cell walls.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a cream or solution that you put directly on your skin. Wash and dry the affected skin area completely before applying. Use a small amount and gently rub it into the skin and the area around the infection. Wash your hands well before and after applying, unless you are treating your hands. Do not get this medicine in your eyes, mouth, nose, or vagina. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or wrapping unless your doctor tells you to. Use this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed, even if your skin starts to feel better early.
dosing: Apply the cream or solution to the affected area once or twice a day, as directed by your doctor. The length of treatment depends on the type of infection. Ringworm and jock itch are usually treated for 3 to 4 weeks. Athlete's foot may need up to 4 to 6 weeks of treatment. Tinea versicolor is usually treated for 3 to 4 weeks. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze the cream or solution. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If this happens, rinse well with water right away. Avoid wearing tight-fitting, synthetic (non-breathable) clothing over the treated area, as this can make the infection worse. For infections in the groin or foot area, wear clean, loose-fitting cotton clothing and socks. Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or shoes with others, as fungal infections can spread. Do not use this medicine on children under 12 years old unless told to by a doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if: your skin becomes more red, swollen, itchy, or irritated after using this medicine; you develop a rash, blistering, or burning that is severe; your infection does not improve after 4 weeks of treatment; or you think you may be having an allergic reaction (signs include severe rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing — call 911 or go to the emergency room right away for these symptoms).
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. However, it is very important to keep using the medicine for the full length of time your doctor prescribed, even if you feel better. Stopping too early can allow the fungus to come back. Full clearing of the infection may take 3 to 6 weeks depending on the type of infection.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children under 12 years old unless directed by a doctor. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are usually needed for older adults, but tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and other medicines you take.
